definitionEn: a state in which plans, aims or groups agree with and support each other
senseNote: Здесь — «согласованность, соответствие» целей и позиций; техническое «выравнивание» (колёс, текста) не тренируем.
situation: Talking about whether a team's goals, a company's actions or people's views agree and support each other.

examples.text: There is little [[alignment]] between what the sales team promises and what the product can do.
The two parties are in close [[alignment]] on climate policy, which makes a coalition likely.
The inspectors praised the strong [[alignment]] between what is taught in class and what is tested in exams.

texts: Regular meetings keep the design and engineering teams in [[alignment]].
Voters expect some [[alignment]] between a candidate's promises and actions.
The new tax brings the country into [[alignment]] with its neighbours.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Выравнивание доходов» — income equalisation или narrowing the income gap. Alignment — согласованность целей и позиций, а не уравнивание.

collocationTask.explanationRu: In alignment with (как и in line with) — «в соответствии с». Correspondence — «переписка», equality — «равенство», similarity — «сходство»; в этом обороте они не работают.

nuance.text: There is a clear [[alignment]] between the company's prices and its premium image.
nuance.explanationRu: Alignment — соответствие, согласованность (цен и имиджа, целей и действий). Alliance — союз стран, партий или компаний; между ценой и имиджем союза быть не может.

reverse.text: The three charities have formed an [[alliance]] to share offices and staff.
reverse.explanationRu: Официальный союз организаций — an alliance (form an alliance). Alignment — не союз, а согласованность целей или позиций.

fixIt.text: There is little [[accordance]] between the brand's green image and its actual practices.
fixIt.explanationRu: Accordance живёт только в обороте in accordance with. Соответствие между имиджем и реальными делами — alignment.

wordFormation.text: The merger failed partly because of poor [[alignment]] between the two company cultures.

definitionEn: used after two groups to mean both of them equally
senseNote: Здесь — «и те и другие, в равной мере» (X and Y alike), а не просто «похожи» (they look alike).
situation: Saying that something affects or pleases two different groups equally, for example experts and beginners.

examples.text: The night market is popular with tourists and locals [[alike]].
Teachers and parents [[alike]] have complained that the new grading system is confusing.
Her debut novel won praise from critics and ordinary readers [[alike]].

texts: The exhibition fascinates children and adults [[alike]].
Rising rents affect students and young families [[alike]].
The new rules apply to managers and junior staff [[alike]].

badCollocation.noteRu: «Одинаково важный» — equally important. Alike ставят после двух групп людей (teachers and parents alike), а не перед прилагательным.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Young and old alike — «и молодые, и пожилые». Likewise и similarly не ставят после пары существительных, а same без the так не употребляют.

nuance.text: The storm damaged expensive villas and small cottages [[alike]].
nuance.explanationRu: Alike стоит сразу после двух групп: villas and cottages alike — «и те и другие». Likewise значит «так же, аналогично» и после пары существительных не ставится.

reverse.text: My sister became a doctor, and her husband did [[likewise]].
reverse.explanationRu: Did likewise — «поступил так же». Alike в этом значении с do не употребляют.

fixIt.text: This podcast is popular with scientists and ordinary listeners [[both]].
fixIt.explanationRu: После пары существительных «и те и другие» передают словом alike. Both ставят перед парой: both scientists and ordinary listeners.

reply.context: A friend asks: "Is the new science museum worth visiting if I don't have kids?"
options: Not really. The exhibits are alike for adults, so you'd get bored.
Indubitably; the establishment caters to juveniles and adults alike.
Definitely! It's designed for children and adults alike, and the space section is amazing.
reply.explanationRu: Alike после двух групп значит «и те и другие в равной мере». В первом ответе alike употреблено бессмысленно, а второй звучит напыщенно для разговора с другом.

definitionEn: a claim that someone has done something wrong, made without proof
situation: Reporting that someone has been publicly accused of wrongdoing, although nothing has been proved yet.

examples.text: The singer has denied [[allegations]] that she copied the melody from an unknown band.
The university is investigating an [[allegation]] of bullying made by a junior researcher.
Several patients have made [[allegations]] of negligence against the clinic's chief surgeon.

texts: The minister has strongly denied the [[allegations]] against her.
Journalists must check [[allegations]] carefully before publishing them.
The company says the [[allegations]] of pollution are unfounded.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Обвинение в мошенничестве» — an allegation of fraud. Предлог in здесь — калька с русского.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Отрицать обвинения — deny the allegations (или reject them). Refuse и decline — «отказываться» от предложения, negate — «сводить на нет».

nuance.text: The newspaper published [[allegations]] that the mayor had accepted gifts from builders.
nuance.explanationRu: Allegation — обвинение, которое кто-то высказывает публично, без доказательств, например в газете. Charge — официальное обвинение полиции или прокурора; газеты его не выдвигают.

reverse.text: He pleaded not guilty to both [[charges]] at the first hearing.
reverse.explanationRu: В суде признают или не признают вину по официальным обвинениям — charges. Allegations — обвинения в прессе или жалобах, до суда.

fixIt.text: The director denied all the [[blames]] made against him in the press.
fixIt.explanationRu: Blame — неисчисляемое «вина», во множественном числе не употребляется. Публичные обвинения в прессе — allegations.

wordFormation.text: She made a serious [[allegation]] against her former employer.

reply.context: A colleague whispers: "Someone says the finance director has been taking money from the company."
options: It's only an allegation so far. Let's not judge him until there's an investigation.
Then it's an allegation, which means he's definitely guilty.
Such allegations must be substantiated forthwith by the relevant parties, dear colleague.
reply.explanationRu: Allegation — обвинение без доказательств, поэтому оно не доказывает вину. Третий ответ звучит как официальный документ, а не реплика в разговоре.

definitionEn: to state that someone did something wrong without giving proof
situation: Reporting a serious claim about wrongdoing, especially in news or court, before anyone has proved it.

examples.text: The lawsuit [[alleges]] that the landlord ignored repeated complaints about damp.
Two former employees have [[alleged]] that they were paid less than male colleagues and are suing the firm.
The player is [[alleged]] to have accepted money to lose the match.

texts: The report [[alleged]] that safety checks had been skipped.
Critics have [[alleged]] that the contest was fixed.
She [[alleged]] that her neighbour had damaged her car.

badCollocation.noteRu: Allege не строится как accuse: нельзя allege someone of something. Говорят allege that he committed fraud или accuse him of fraud.

collocationTask.prompt: It is ___ that the director hid the losses.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Безличное «утверждается, что» — it is alleged that. С accuse и blame нужен человек (accuse someone of), а complain так не употребляют.

nuance.text: The article [[alleges]] that the factory has been dumping waste into the river.
nuance.explanationRu: Allege сочетается с that: alleges that the factory has been dumping waste. Accuse требует дополнения и предлога of: accuses the factory of dumping waste.

reverse.text: My neighbour [[accused]] me of stealing her parking space.
reverse.explanationRu: Обвинить кого-то в чём-то — accuse someone of something. Allege так не строится: alleged me of — ошибка.

fixIt.text: The newspaper [[pretends]] that the minister knew about the problem months ago.
fixIt.explanationRu: Pretend — «притворяться». Если газета утверждает что-то без доказательств, нужно alleges that.

rewrite.original: People say, without any proof, that the manager lied to investors.
rewrite.explanationRu: Be alleged to have done — «по утверждениям, сделал (но это не доказано)».

definitionEn: according to what people claim, although it has not been proved
situation: Reporting what someone is said to have done, while making clear it has not been proved.

examples.text: Nothing has been proved yet, but the director [[allegedly]] hid the losses from investors.
My neighbour's cat [[allegedly]] ate a whole chicken, but nobody actually saw it happen.
The painting was [[allegedly]] stolen from a castle during the war, though no records survive.

texts: The documents were [[allegedly]] leaked by a junior employee.
The restaurant [[allegedly]] reused bread from customers' plates.
He [[allegedly]] lied about his age to join the army.

badCollocation.noteRu: Перед существительным нужно прилагательное: the alleged thief. Allegedly — наречие: he allegedly stole the money.

collocationTask.prompt: The money was ___ stolen by a former employee.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Allegedly — «якобы, по чьим-то словам». Admittedly — «надо признать», accordingly — «соответственно», arguably — «пожалуй, можно утверждать».

nuance.text: The two officials [[allegedly]] accepted bribes, and their trial begins next month.
nuance.explanationRu: Allegedly — осторожное слово юристов и журналистов о предполагаемых преступлениях до суда. Apparently — разговорное «похоже, говорят»; в новости о суде оно звучит небрежно.

reverse.text: [[Apparently]], the new café on the corner does amazing pancakes.
reverse.explanationRu: Пересказать приятный слух — apparently («говорят»). Allegedly намекает на недоказанное обвинение и про блинчики звучит странно.

fixIt.text: The accountant [[as if]] moved the money to a secret account.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Якобы» не переводится как as if: as if — «как будто» в сравнениях. О недоказанных обвинениях говорят allegedly.

wordFormation.text: The actor was [[allegedly]] paid twice for the same advertisement.

reply.context: Your friend texts: "Is it true that the new gym manager was fired for stealing?"
options: Yes, he allegedly stole it. I watched him take the cash on camera myself.
Nobody knows for sure. He allegedly took money from the till, but nothing's been proved.
It is alleged, by persons unknown, that the gentleman misappropriated funds.
reply.explanationRu: Allegedly — «якобы, по чьим-то словам, но не доказано». Если вы сами всё видели, allegedly не нужно. Третий ответ звучит как протокол, а не сообщение другу.

rewrite.original: According to some people, the mayor used public money for his holiday, but this hasn't been proved.
rewrite.frame: The mayor ____ used public money for his holiday.
rewrite.explanationRu: Allegedly — «якобы»: о том, что утверждают, но не доказали.

definitionEn: to make pain, suffering or a problem less severe
situation: Talking about making pain, stress, poverty or another problem less serious, though not removing it completely.

examples.text: Gentle stretching can [[alleviate]] back pain caused by sitting at a desk all day.
The new bridge was built to [[alleviate]] traffic congestion in the city centre.
Flexible hours have helped [[alleviate]] stress among staff with young children.

texts: This cream should [[alleviate]] the itching within minutes.
Extra funding could [[alleviate]] the shortage of teachers.
Nothing she said could [[alleviate]] his fears about the operation.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Облегчить задачу» — make the task easier или simplify it. Alleviate смягчает боль, страдания и проблемы, а не задания.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Облегчить симптомы — alleviate (или relieve) the symptoms. Lighten — «делать легче по весу или светлее», soften — «смягчать» материал или тон, facilitate — «содействовать».

nuance.text: Regular breaks can [[alleviate]] eye strain for people who work at screens.
nuance.explanationRu: Оба слова переводят как «облегчать», но alleviate — ослаблять боль или проблему, а facilitate — делать процесс проще. Facilitate eye strain означало бы «способствовать» усталости глаз.

reverse.text: The new software will [[facilitate]] communication between the two offices.
reverse.explanationRu: Облегчить, упростить процесс — facilitate. Alleviate ослабляет что-то плохое, а общение — не проблема.

fixIt.text: The doctor gave her some tablets to [[lighten]] the pain in her knee.
fixIt.explanationRu: Lighten — «делать легче по весу или светлее». Облегчить боль — alleviate the pain.

wordFormation.text: The charity focuses on the [[alleviation]] of hunger in rural areas.

reply.context: A colleague says: "I've had a terrible headache all morning, and my presentation is at three."
options: Oh no! Staring at your screen all day will alleviate it even more.
Kindly procure an analgesic to alleviate the aforementioned discomfort.
Try drinking some water and getting some fresh air. That might alleviate it a bit.
reply.explanationRu: Alleviate — ослабить боль, а не усилить её, так что первый ответ нелогичен. Второй звучит как инструкция к лекарству, а не совет коллеге.

rewrite.original: Talking to a counsellor has made her anxiety less severe.
rewrite.frame: Talking to a counsellor has ____ her anxiety.
rewrite.explanationRu: Alleviate — сделать боль, тревогу или проблему слабее.

definitionEn: an agreement between countries, groups or companies to work together
situation: Talking about countries, parties or companies that agree to cooperate because they share goals or enemies.

examples.text: The two airlines formed an [[alliance]] so that passengers could book connecting flights more easily.
In an unlikely [[alliance]], farmers and environmental groups campaigned together against the new motorway.
In the reality show, contestants form secret [[alliances]] to avoid being voted off.

texts: The small party refused to enter an [[alliance]] with its old rivals.
Several hospitals have formed an [[alliance]] to share expensive equipment.
The two kingdoms sealed their [[alliance]] with a royal marriage.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Профсоюз» — a trade union. Alliance — союз стран, партий или компаний, а не организация работников.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Заключить союз — form (или forge) an alliance. Do, take и open с alliance не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The three countries remain independent but have formed a defensive [[alliance]].
nuance.explanationRu: Alliance — союз самостоятельных сторон ради общей цели. Union — объединение в единое целое (the European Union, a trade union), и с remain independent оно спорит.

reverse.text: She is an active member of the teachers' [[union]].
reverse.explanationRu: Профсоюз — union (the teachers' union, a trade union). Слово alliance для профсоюзов не используют.

fixIt.text: The two companies have entered into a strategic [[union]] to develop electric vans.
fixIt.explanationRu: Союз компаний ради общей цели — a strategic alliance. Union — полное слияние в одно целое или профсоюз.

wordFormation.text: The small shops on our street have formed an [[alliance]] to compete with the supermarket.

definitionEn: to officially give money, time or resources for a particular purpose
situation: Deciding officially how much money, time, space or staff will go to each project, person or purpose.

examples.text: The council has [[allocated]] an extra two million pounds to school repairs.
On their first day, new employees are [[allocated]] a desk, a laptop and a locker by the office manager.
During exams, try to [[allocate]] your time according to how many marks each question is worth.

texts: Each student is [[allocated]] a personal tutor in the first week.
Funds were [[allocated]] to rebuild the damaged bridge.
We were [[allocated]] a table right next to the kitchen door.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Выделить главную мысль» — highlight или identify the main idea. Allocate — выделять деньги, время или ресурсы.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Выделить деньги — allocate funds. Select («отобрать»), distinguish («отличить») и extract («извлечь») тоже бывают «выделить», но к деньгам не подходят.

nuance.text: The school has [[allocated]] five thousand pounds for new books but has not bought any yet.
nuance.explanationRu: Allocate — выделить, зарезервировать деньги на цель. Spend — реально потратить; «потратили, но ничего не купили» — противоречие.

reverse.text: We [[spent]] far too much on the taxi from the airport.
reverse.explanationRu: Потратить деньги на что-то — spend on. Allocate — заранее выделить средства по плану; о тратах на такси так не говорят.

fixIt.text: The government will [[highlight]] extra money for rural hospitals next year.
fixIt.explanationRu: Highlight — «выделять, подчёркивать» в тексте или речи. Выделить деньги — allocate money.

reply.context: Your boss asks: "How are you planning to prepare for next month's conference?"
options: I've allocated two full days next week just for writing the slides.
I've allocated the slides, so they're completely finished now.
Gonna allocate some time or whatever, dunno yet.
reply.explanationRu: Allocate time for something — выделить время на задачу. Allocate не значит «закончить», а третий ответ слишком небрежен для разговора с начальником.

definitionEn: an amount of money, space or time officially given for a purpose
situation: Talking about how money, seats, tickets or time are officially shared out, or the share each person gets.

examples.text: The [[allocation]] of funds between schools has been criticised as unfair to rural areas.
Each club receives a ticket [[allocation]] of about three thousand seats for away matches.
Staff complained that the [[allocation]] of parking spaces favoured senior managers.

texts: The hospital's budget [[allocation]] was cut by ten per cent.
Seat [[allocation]] for the exam is done by surname.
Each country's fishing [[allocation]] is agreed every December.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Выделение тепла» — the release of heat. Allocation — распределение денег, мест или времени, а не физический процесс.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Справедливое распределение ресурсов — a fair allocation of resources. Location — «местоположение», separation — «разделение», isolation — «изоляция».

nuance.text: The government announced a larger [[allocation]] of funds for flood defences.
nuance.explanationRu: Allocation — распределение бюджета между целями и проектами. Allowance — положенная человеку сумма или норма (baggage allowance, travel allowance); к бюджету на защиту от наводнений не подходит.

reverse.text: Business-class tickets come with a bigger baggage [[allowance]].
reverse.explanationRu: Норма багажа пассажира — baggage allowance. Allocation — распределение ресурсов, а не личная норма.

fixIt.text: The [[selection]] of funds for the new stadium was approved by the city council.
fixIt.explanationRu: Selection — «выбор, отбор». Выделение денег на проект — allocation of funds.

wordFormation.text: Teachers are unhappy about the [[allocation]] of classrooms for next term.

definitionEn: an amount of money or something else that you are officially permitted
senseNote: Здесь — «положенная норма или выплата» (baggage allowance, travel allowance), а не карманные деньги ребёнка.
situation: Talking about the fixed amount of money, luggage, data or holiday you are officially entitled to.

examples.text: My suitcase was three kilos over the baggage [[allowance]], so I had to pay extra.
Employees who travel for work receive a daily [[allowance]] for meals and taxis.
I used up my entire mobile data [[allowance]] watching films on the train.

texts: Students can apply for a housing [[allowance]] if they live away from home.
The recommended daily [[allowance]] of salt is about six grams.
Check the luggage [[allowance]] before you book a budget flight.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Разрешение уйти пораньше» — permission to leave early. Allowance — положенная сумма или норма, а не разрешение.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Норма провоза багажа — baggage allowance. Norm — «норма поведения», permission — «разрешение», standard — «стандарт качества».

nuance.text: On top of her salary, she gets a monthly [[allowance]] for childcare.
nuance.explanationRu: Allowance — дополнительная выплата на конкретные расходы: жильё, питание, детский сад. Wage — оплата за сам труд, и зарплату «на детский сад» не выдают.

reverse.text: Cleaners at the hotel earn the minimum [[wage]].
reverse.explanationRu: Минимальная оплата труда — the minimum wage. Allowance — не зарплата, а положенная доплата или норма.

fixIt.text: Economy passengers have a hand luggage [[norm]] of seven kilos.
fixIt.explanationRu: Norm — «норма поведения» или «стандарт». Разрешённый вес ручной клади — hand luggage allowance.

wordFormation.text: The company pays each employee a generous travel [[allowance]] for conferences abroad.

reply.context: Your friend is packing: "Can I take this huge suitcase on the plane for free?"
options: Sure, the allowance means you can take as much luggage as you like.
Check your ticket first. Budget airlines often include only a small cabin bag in the allowance.
Pursuant to the carrier's regulations, one's allowance is strictly delimited.
reply.explanationRu: Allowance — это ограниченная норма, а не «сколько угодно». Третий ответ звучит как юридический документ, а не совет другу.

rewrite.original: Passengers on this flight may bring up to twenty kilos of luggage free of charge.
rewrite.frame: The luggage ____ on this flight is twenty kilos.
